description: This file contains JUnit test cases for the CommandConsumerFactoryImpl class in the org.eclipse.hono.client.impl package. It tests the creation, error handling, reconnection, and lifecycle management of command consumer links over a messaging connection, including handling remote close events and connection failures.

classes.name: CommandConsumerFactoryImplTest
classes.description: JUnit test suite for testing the CommandConsumerFactoryImpl class, including connection handling, link creation, error cases, and lifecycle management.

methods.name: setUp
methods.description: Prepares the test fixture by initializing mock objects and configuring their behavior before each test.

methods.name: testCreateCommandConsumerFailsIfPeerRejectsLink
methods.description: Verifies that creating a command consumer fails gracefully if the peer rejects to open a receiver link.

methods.name: testCreateCommandConsumerSucceeds
methods.description: Ensures that a command consumer is successfully created for a given tenant and device ID, and the link opens correctly.

methods.name: testCreateCommandConsumerSetsRemoteCloseHandler
methods.description: Checks that when a command consumer link is closed remotely, the provided close handler is invoked.

methods.name: testCreateCommandConsumerWithGatewaySetsRemoteCloseHandler
methods.description: Verifies that close handlers are correctly invoked for gateway-associated command consumers upon remote link closure.

methods.name: testLocalCloseRemovesCommandConsumerFromCache
methods.description: Tests that closing a command consumer locally removes it from cache, cancels liveness checks, and allows recreation.

methods.name: testConsumerIsRecreatedOnConnectionFailure
methods.description: Ensures that a command consumer is re-created when the connection is disrupted and subsequently re-established.

methods.name: testLivenessCheckLocksRecreationAttempt
methods.description: Verifies that multiple liveness checks do not trigger concurrent reconnection attempts and that retries are properly handled.
